purpose: Determine whether the PSA PSGC API can independently verify the current 3Q 2026 administrative-registry capture while the official XLSX request is blocked.

sources.title: PSA Statistical Classification Systems API Access Guide
observed: The guide documents the PSGC API base URL as https://classification.psa.gov.ph/psgc.
The guide first states that no authentication is required, but its token-access section says requests must include a token and that users receive one by email after submitting the API request form.
It documents PSGC classification records and JSON responses; it does not document boundary polygon geometry.

sources.title: PSA Philippine Standard Geographic Code API Documentation
observed: The displayed available versions are Q2_2024, April_2024, Q4_2023, and Q2_2021.
The documented levels include regions, provinces, municipalities/cities, and barangays.
No 2026 version is listed in the documentation reviewed on this date.

sources.title: PSA PSGC Summary
observed: The page links the latest release, Third Quarter 2026 PSGC Updates, dated 12 October 2026.
The page labels its publication as Philippine Standard Geographic Code as of 30 September 2026.
The rendered national aggregate reports 82 provinces, 149 cities, 1,493 municipalities, and 42,010 barangays.

whatItCanSupport: Current official national aggregate-count sanity checks from the live summary page.
A future code/name cross-check if PSA confirms an accessible version matching the 30 September 2026 release.
whatItCannotCurrentlySupport: Exact 3Q 2026 row-by-row comparison of the captured directory against a downloaded workbook.
A claim that the documented API contains a current 2026 PSGC version.
Administrative boundary geometry or waterbody geometry.
assessment.reason: The workbook request returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge. The API docs list older versions and are inconsistent about token requirements; no token was requested and no API request was made. The live summary is an aggregate control, not a row-level substitute.
assessment.reuseNote: The PSA website states that site content is CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise stated. API-specific terms were not independently verified; confirm before redistributing API output.
